The root cause of the repeated error is an unterminated f-string in the `print()` statement — specifically, a line break inside an f-string without proper escaping or continuation. This causes a `SyntaxError`.

We will fix the code by splitting the `print` statement into two lines or using a regular string format.

{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
sales = pd.read_csv('/home/musel/Github/research_agent/data/sales.csv')

# Filter out refunded orders
completed_only = sales[sales['status'] == 'completed']

# Filter out QA orders (revenue == '999999.99')
qa_orders = completed_only[completed_only['revenue'] == '999999.99']
print('Number of QA orders in completed set:', len(qa_orders))

# Final population: completed orders, excluding QA (but there are none)
final_data = completed_only

# Check channel distribution
channel_counts = final_data['channel'].value_counts()
print('Channel counts:', channel_counts.to_dict())

# Check conversion rate by channel
conversion_rates = final_data.groupby('channel')['converted'].mean()
print('Conversion rates by channel:')
print(conversion_rates)

# Compute difference
diff = conversion_rates['email'] - conversion_rates['paid_search']
print('Difference (email - paid_search):', diff)"}
